What is HeyGen?

AI avatar video platform strongest at video translation with voice cloning and lip sync - it takes an existing video of a real person and reproduces it in another language in their own voice with matched mouth movement. Also offers avatar generation and interactive avatars.

Best for

Translating existing video into other languages while keeping the original speaker's voice.

Main features

  • Video Translate preserving the speaker's own cloned voice across 175+ languages with lip sync
  • 700+ stock avatars
  • Instant Avatar from a 2-minute webcam recording
  • Avatar IV for photo-to-video animation
  • Interactive Avatar for real-time conversational video
  • Photo Avatar
  • voice cloning
  • templates
  • brand kit
  • API
  • batch generation.

Practical use cases

  • Translating a CEO's announcement into 12 languages in their own voice
  • personalised sales video at scale with the prospect's name
  • creating a spokesperson avatar from a phone recording
  • localising a YouTube channel
  • interactive product demos.

Who is it for?

  • Marketers, creators, sales teams doing personalised outreach, e-learning producers and companies localising video content.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium credit-based subscription; enterprise licensing

Plans described in the source

Free with roughly 3 videos per month, up to 3 minutes each, watermarked. Creator around $29/mo ($24 annually) with unlimited video length on some plans and no watermark. Team around $89-99/seat/mo ($69 annually) with more credits, brand kit and collaboration. Enterprise custom, annual, with API volume, SSO and dedicated avatars. Video Translate and Interactive Avatar are metered separately by minute on most tiers.

Free plan

Yes - free tier with roughly 3 watermarked videos per month.

Free trial

Free tier serves as the trial; enterprise trials via sales.

Usage limits to consider

Credit and minute metered. Video translation minutes are charged separately from avatar generation credits. Instant Avatar creation is limited by tier. Free tier is watermarked and capped at 3 videos/month.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Video Translate with voice cloning and lip sync is the standout capability here - keeping the original speaker's voice across languages is far more persuasive than a stock avatar
  • Instant Avatar from a 2-minute webcam recording lowers the barrier dramatically
  • API-first design makes personalised video at scale practical
  • faster and cheaper than Synthesia for many use cases.

Limitations to consider

  • Voice cloning raises serious consent and deepfake concerns - HeyGen has controls but the misuse risk is real and organisations need a policy
  • enterprise compliance documentation is thinner than Synthesia
  • translation quality varies notably by language pair
  • credit and minute metering across two separate pools is confusing
  • occasional uncanny artefacts in lip sync.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, iOS, Android
  • API
  • Chrome extension

Languages

  • 175+ languages for translation including Arabic and French - broader than Synthesia for the translate feature specifically

API access

Yes - HeyGen API with generous documentation, priced per credit; widely used for programmatic personalised video

Integrations and exports

  • Zapier, HubSpot, Salesforce, Canva, Descript, Slack, Google Drive, API-first design for embedding

Evaluation notes

Establish a written consent policy before cloning any employee's voice or likeness - this is a legal exposure, not just an ethical one, and jurisdictions differ. Test Arabic translation output with native speakers; quality is good but not uniform.
